title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
why: A frontier VLM planner (gpt-5.6-sol via Codex) is wrapped in an editable harness that maintains task context, checks commands and applies execution-control rules over a frozen VLA executor; the harness itself is revised by rollout-driven self-evolution (diagnosis agent → revision agent → rollout verifier) and frozen before held-out testing. Directly on the harness-self-optimisation axis for embodied manipulation.
mechanism: Harness layer between VLM planner and fixed VLA: episode guidance, runtime task context (progress summary, facts, outcomes, uncertainty, stagnation control state), action-candidate retrieval from the executor's command set, response checks and control rules. Self-evolution edits three harness components (planning guidance, assessment criteria, control rules) using failure diagnosis on recorded traces; a verifier compares candidates against cached baseline outcomes on the same episodes and selects; selected config fixed before held-out test. No VLM or VLA weight updates.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: RoboMME (16 history-dependent tasks, 4 suites), 50 episodes per task (800 total), simulator success; compared against VLA, memory-augmented (SAM2Act, FrameSamp+Modul) and hierarchical (SimpleSG/GroundSG, MemER) baselines taken from the official leaderboard; with vs. without self-evolution ablation; exploratory RoboMemArena development runs. Gains attributable to harness revision vs. planner budget need checking (frontier planner vs. leaderboard baselines).
evidence_locator: arXiv abs; HTML v1 §3.2–3.3 (harness, self-evolution), §4.1–4.4, Table 1, Fig. 3
retrieval_notes: Read abstract and HTML method/experiment sections. Appendix A/B (panel construction, selection rules, per-task counts, whether revision episodes overlap test seeds) not read in detail; no code link found on abs page.

title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments
why: Provides TARSphere-Harness, an embodied brain harness that lets frozen MLLMs act through multi-level executable skills with hierarchical memory and execution feedback, plus a physics-simulated benchmark (TARSphere-Bench) with event-driven FSM outcome checking; evaluates 8 MLLMs under one harness. Both A-type harness and B-type benchmark contribution.
mechanism: Harness: serial action execution that can return control at tool boundaries; observations = egocentric RGB, body-frame LiDAR, public events, execution feedback incl. motion residuals and collision bearings; memory = short-term history, long-term plan/dialogue/robot-state records, semantic spatial memory grounded in RGB-D, self-managed key memory; unified skill interface (body/gaze/end-effector primitives, grasp skills, navigation to points/frontiers/remembered entities, social actions with spatial preconditions); controller backends swappable for VLN/VLA policies. Infra: physics sim with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue; event-driven FSM updates task state and evaluates outcomes.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: 360 episodes across 30 GRScenes-100 scenes, two task families (navigate-and-report, fetch-and-deliver) × Base + five paired conditions (perceptual robustness, disruption adaptation, task update, human coordination, intent understanding); 8 frozen MLLMs (4 proprietary, 2 general open, 2 embodied open) with shared prompts/observations/actions, 100-decision cap; staged progress/success metrics, path efficiency, collision/fall incidence, decision/token cost; harness ablations (motion residuals, LiDAR, memory, skills), controlled intervention study, failure analysis, execution checks, curation ablations, human evaluation. Note: part of the scoring uses continuous quality scores for plans/reports—judge mechanism needs auditing.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs (comments: 13 pages, code link); HTML v1 §3.2.2, §3.3, §4.1, Table 2 caption, §4.3 headings
retrieval_notes: Read abstract, harness and setup sections. How plan/inspection/report quality is scored (LLM judge vs. rule) and benchmark curation details not verified.

title: From Reasoning to Action: Benchmarking Frontier AI Models on LIBERO-10 Robot Manipulation Tasks
why: Controlled closed-loop evaluation of six frontier models directly controlling a Franka arm in LIBERO-10 through a minimal tool-call harness (end-effector pose targets + gripper), with reasoning-effort sweeps and cost—an evaluation-methodology/baseline lead for harness-vs-model attribution.
mechanism: Minimal harness: observations (camera images, proprioception) and interaction history in prompt; three native function-calling tools, one call per turn (move_to with 10-D target pose, plus done / give_up requiring a 'hindsight' note); adapter interpolates straight-line end-effector trajectories at 20 Hz into LIBERO OSC commands; no task-specific fine-tuning or pretrained skills; hindsight notes logged but never fed back (zero-shot).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: LIBERO-10, 6 models × 3 reasoning-effort levels = 18 configurations, 1,800 episodes; success from LIBERO's per-step goal-predicate checker on simulator state (episode ends immediately on success); inference cost vs. effort; per-task and failure analysis from model hindsight.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs (technical report, 17 pages, code link); HTML v1 §2.1–2.3 (tools, hindsight, move_to execution, per-step success check, termination), §3 headings
retrieval_notes: Read abstract and framework sections. Per-task tables and episode counts per task/config not re-checked. Technical report (UT Dallas IRVL), not peer-reviewed.

title: Plan First, Act Later: Streaming Reasoning for Executable Memory in Robot Control
why: Hierarchical VLM-over-VLA control where the VLM writes an executable subtask_list and semantic-event memory from streaming observations, then selects the current subtask for a low-level VLA; the memory-writing VLM is trained with a two-stage data pipeline including self-labeling with task-grounded verification on the deployment state distribution (on-policy-style correction of the high-level planner).
mechanism: High level: fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-4B (LoRA) maintaining short-term visual buffer, semantic-event memory and executable subtask_list; low level: pretrained MemER VLA (same as MemER baseline). Training: Stage 1 expands sparse memory-update supervision; Stage 2 self-labels rollouts with task-grounded verification to match execution-time state distribution. Baseline 'GPT-6-astra + VLA' swaps PAL's VLM for a frontier model with the same interface.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: RoboMME memory-dependent benchmark, 50 episodes per task per seed, vs. MemER, FrameSamp+Modul and GPT-6-astra+VLA; ablations of the training stages; real-world Franka Research 3 on four manipulation tasks with difficulty levels, vs. MemER and FrameSamp-Modul.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs; HTML v1 §4–5 headings, Appendix B.1 Table 4, C.3, D.2
retrieval_notes: Read abstract, architecture table and evaluation-protocol paragraphs. Real-world trial counts per task and whether self-labeling tasks overlap evaluation tasks not verified. Project URL on abs page not resolved.

title: CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning
why: Non-parametric memory/skill-knowledge layer for MLLM embodied planners: distils interaction experience into action-centred precondition/effect knowledge over a factorized world state, then grounds it at planning time for backward/forward reasoning; improves closed-loop replanning across frozen backbones without weight updates.
mechanism: Factorized world-state representation (object attributes, inter-object relations) built from observations; action-centred causal knowledge library constructed from interaction experience; task-time causal backward retrieval + semantic retrieval grounded in current observation for action selection, multi-step planning, recovery and verification. Planner backbones frozen (Qwen3.5-9B/27B/35B-A3B main; InternVL3.5 and Gemma4 for cross-family).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: adapted VirtualHome (visual planning interface), RoboCasa one-shot planning and closed-loop replanning, SWITCH interaction-reasoning accuracy, real-robot sequential manipulation; same backbone/observations/action space across methods; baselines Vanilla, SelfReVision, LookPlanGraph; component, retrieval-path and precondition-vs-effect ablations; 100 held-out test cases mentioned in an appendix. VirtualHome uses an observation-repair step with an image-editing model—needs audit.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs (project page https://causground.github.io); HTML v1 §4 headings, §4.1 setup paragraph, Tables 1–2 text, Appendix C.1, D
retrieval_notes: Read abstract, setup and ablation text. Separation between library-construction episodes and test episodes, and real-robot trial counts, not verified.

title: SLoSa: Small, Low-Power, and Safe Foundation Models for Robotic Task Planning
why: Distils a safety-aware robot task planner from a pipeline of classical planners, a teacher LLM (GPT-5.4-mini) and formal verifiers into compact 4B–14B LLMs via SFT, then RL with a verification-based reward machine; deployed INT4 on Jetson Orin and a desktop arm. Fits teacher/verifier-to-student distillation and verifier-reward RL for embodied planners.
mechanism: Data: classical planners + teacher LLM + formal validator generate safety-constrained plans; training: SFT then GRPO-style RL with verification-based reward machine enforcing safety constraints; backbones Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-14B (and Llama-8B for efficiency); local INT4 inference.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: four PDDL domains (manipulation, transportation, object transfer, tool use) with formal-validator success; directly prompted GPT-5.6 Sol / Claude Sonnet 5 as comparisons; positive-only data ablation; separately trained planners on safety-adapted VirtualHome and ALFWorld; RTX 4080 / Jetson Orin power/latency; desktop robotic arm demonstration. Most success is plan-level (validator), not closed-loop execution—evidence likely offline except household-sim/robot parts.
evidence_locator: arXiv abs; HTML v1 §IV–V (data construction, backbones, Tables III–V text)
retrieval_notes: Scope borderline: compact planner rather than a full harness loop; kept because of teacher+verifier distillation and verifier-reward RL. Physical-robot protocol (trials, tasks) not read; no code link.

title: Agentic World Action Models
why: AW-0 couples a code expert (parameterized skill routines and control logic) with video and action experts in one mixture-of-transformers world action model, and curates trajectories into reusable program skill libraries for subsequent agentic execution—a code-as-policy/skill-library mechanism internalised into a WAM. Borderline vs. 'pure VLA' exclusion; needs full read to decide whether a harness loop exists.
mechanism: Three coupled generative streams (code, future video, robot actions) with joint denoising; agentic coding inside the WAM; automated agentic annotation pipeline labels robot and human videos with aligned programs and consolidates routines into skill libraries; hybrid-action execution.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: RoboTwin 2.0 and physical bimanual tasks (YAM, Tianji–Sharpa) vs. VLA and WAM baselines; language following, semantic reasoning, robustness, ablations. Numbers not copied.

title: OMAR: Open-World Multi-Attribute Reasoning for Scene-Conditioned Shelf Organization
why: Modular VLM+LLM pipeline for robots: VLM proposes labels/attributes grounded via segmentation, depth and multi-view association into an instance-level 3D scene graph, LLM infers latent shelf organization and ranks placements, followed by geometric/kinematic feasibility checks before execution—perception-as-tools plus pre-execution verification.
mechanism: VLM attribute proposal → grounding tools (segmentation, depth, multi-view association) → 3D scene graph → LLM placement reasoning/ranking → feasibility checks → execution.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: instance mapping and placement coherence vs. single-view language-grounding and geometry-only baselines; autonomous placement of unseen objects. Whether closed-loop execution success with trial counts is reported is not known.
retrieval_notes: Abstract only; experiment section (V) not read; no code link.
